caption: Figure 1. ReLU vs. PReLU. For PReLU, the coefficient of the negative part is not constant and is adaptively learned.
description:
Figure type: Line graph
Description: The figure displays two line graphs comparing ReLU and PReLU functions. In the left graph, the ReLU function is depicted with f(y) = 0 for y < 0 and f(y) = y for y ≥ 0. The right graph shows the PReLU function with f(y) = 0 for y < 0, f(y) = y for y ≥ 0, and an adaptive coefficient a for the negative part.

caption: Figure 2. The convergence of a 22-layer large model (B in Table 3). The x-axis is the number of training epochs. The y-axis is the top-1 error of 3,000 random val samples, evaluated on the center crop. We use ReLU as the activation for both cases. Both our initialization (red) and ' Xavier ' (blue) [7] lead to convergence, but ours starts reducing error earlier.
description:
Description: The figure is a line graph comparing the convergence of two different initialization methods for a 22-layer model. The x-axis represents the number of training epochs, and the y-axis shows the top-1 error of 3,000 random validation samples. The red line represents the authors' initialization method, while the blue line represents the Xavier initialization. The red line starts reducing error earlier and remains lower throughout the epochs.

Text in figure: Error, Epoch, 1/n_Var[w] = 1 ours, 1/n_Var[w] = 1 Xavier.

caption: Figure 3. The convergence of a 30-layer small model (see the main text). We use ReLU as the activation for both cases. Our initialization (red) is able to make it converge. But ' Xavier ' (blue) [7] completely stalls - we also verify that its gradients are all diminishing. It does not converge even given more epochs.
description:
Figure: Line graph comparing the convergence of two models using different initialization methods.

Description: The graph shows the error rate over epochs for two models. The red line represents the model with the authors' initialization method, while the blue line represents the model with Xavier initialization. The red line starts higher but quickly decreases and remains lower throughout the epochs, indicating better convergence. The blue line, representing Xavier initialization, shows no significant improvement and remains stagnant.

Text in figure: Error, Epoch, 1/n_Var[w] = 1 ours, 1/n_Var[w] = 1 Xavier
